issues.description: Removal of category__in badge config silently breaks active-filter badges for the new category filter
issues.detail: DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES had an entry for filterKey 'category__in' which was deleted in this diff, but the new findings page exposes a Category filter via FilterType.CATEGORY. The PR description explicitly claims 'Active Filter Badges: Generic reusable component for displaying active filters with clear functionality' yet the only category-specific badge config was removed. Unless the new generic component handles category badges via labelFormatter automatically, active category filters will no longer surface a badge — directly contradicting the stated behavior. Verify a category filter still renders a badge with a human-readable label.

issues.description: SEVERITY_ORDER now has duplicate value 4 for both 'Informational' and 'Info'
issues.detail: Adding 'Info: 4' alongside 'Informational: 4' creates two keys mapping to the same ordinal. If any sort/compare logic iterates Object.entries(SEVERITY_ORDER) or uses the inverse map (ordinal -> name), this introduces ambiguity. The proper fix is to normalize the incoming severity string to a canonical form rather than dual-key the constant. Trace all consumers of SEVERITY_ORDER to confirm no inverse lookup or set-based assumption is broken.

issues.description: getCategoryLabel loses canonical labels for known categories (e.g. 'trustboundaries' -> 'Trustboundaries' instead of 'Trust Boundaries')
issues.detail: The previous adapter had an explicit CATEGORY_LABELS map. The new lib/categories.ts replaces that with pure heuristics: split on '-', length<=3 -> uppercase, else capitalize-first. For IDs without hyphens like 'trustboundaries' the new function returns 'Trustboundaries' rather than the previous 'Trust Boundaries'. Similarly 'forensics-ready' still works but any single-token compound (e.g. 'publiclyaccessible' if the API ever returns it) would degrade. Either (a) re-introduce the explicit label map as the first lookup before heuristics, or (b) confirm the API will never return un-hyphenated compound IDs.

issues.description: Acronym heuristic miscapitalizes words like 'AWS' subcomponents and 'TLS' when length > 3 (e.g., 'logging' is fine, but real acronyms longer than 3 chars like 'HTTPS', 'OAuth', 'SAML' would degrade)
issues.detail: The 'length <= 3 means acronym' rule is brittle. Real categories may include longer acronyms (HTTPS, SAML, OAUTH) which would be rendered 'Https', 'Saml', 'Oauth'. Conversely, the short-word rule will uppercase legitimate short non-acronyms (e.g., 'new' -> 'NEW'). Given the SPECIAL_CASES escape hatch is empty, today's known IDs render correctly only by coincidence. Recommend keeping an explicit allow-list of known acronyms in addition to (or instead of) length-based heuristics.

issues.description: CategorySelector uses fixed width 'w-[200px]' which may overflow on small viewports
issues.detail: The trigger is hard-coded to 200px. On mobile/narrow screen the selector may push the 'Risk Radar' title or break the flex layout. Consider 'w-full sm:w-[200px]' or a min/max responsive width. The PR's UI checklist explicitly leaves mobile/tablet/desktop screenshots unchecked, suggesting responsive verification was not performed.

issues.description: HorizontalBarChart recomputes maxValue inside the render loop on every iteration
issues.detail: `const maxValue = data.length > 0 ? Math.max(...data.map((d) => d.value)) : 0;` is inside the `.map` callback over `data`, so it runs N times per render with O(N) cost each — O(N^2) overall. Hoist this above the .map() callback. For typical small N this is invisible but it's an easy fix and was previously also wrong (the prior code computed it inline too, but only when the percentage branch was needed). Same applies to recomputing within each row.

issues.description: displayPercentage rounding differs from bar width calculation, producing visual mismatch
issues.detail: calculatedWidth uses an unrounded ratio (value/maxValue*100), while displayPercentage uses Math.round(value/total*100). They are also computed against different denominators (maxValue vs total). The bar width represents share of the max bar while the displayed number represents share of total — that's a meaningful UX inconsistency. Consider showing both consistently or labeling clearly which metric the % refers to.

issues.description: CategorySelector handleValueChange dead branch: value === '' is unreachable
issues.detail: shadcn Select onValueChange never emits empty string when there's no empty SelectItem — the 'all' SelectItem is what fires. The `value === ''` check is dead code. Minor, but trims confusion.

issues.description: Brand rename 'Threat Score' -> 'Prowler ThreatScore' applied inconsistently across the codebase
issues.detail: The diff updates many user-facing strings but the comment '// ThreatScore colors (0-100 scale, higher = better)' is the only comment updated; other comments, prop names, variable names like THREAT_COLORS, name='Prowler ThreatScore' axis name (which is also a screen-reader concern), and analytics event names (if any) may still reference the old phrasing. Confirm CHANGELOG.md and any docs/i18n strings are aligned. Also confirm marketing/legal owns the exact spelling 'ThreatScore' (one word) — it's an unusual style choice.

issues.description: No unit tests for lib/categories.ts despite checklist claim 'code is being covered by tests'
issues.detail: The diff adds a new pure utility function with non-trivial branching (special cases, regex, length heuristic, default) and no tests are visible in the diff. The checklist box for test coverage is checked. Either add tests for getCategoryLabel covering each rule and edge cases ('iam', 'imdsv1', 'forensics-ready', 'trustboundaries', empty string, all-caps input) or correct the checklist.

issues.description: CategoryId type export removed but may be consumed elsewhere
issues.detail: The adapter previously exported `export type CategoryId = (typeof CATEGORY_IDS)[keyof typeof CATEGORY_IDS];`. The diff removes both CATEGORY_IDS and CategoryId without showing replacements. Any consumer importing CategoryId from this module will fail to typecheck. Grep the codebase for `CategoryId` imports before merge.

dissents.topic: Heuristic-based getCategoryLabel vs explicit label map

positions.position: Heuristics + SPECIAL_CASES escape hatch is fine; covers all current IDs and avoids maintaining a hardcoded map that must be updated alongside the API. When a new category breaks, add a special case.

Replacing a known-correct explicit mapping with heuristics is a regression in determinism. The previous code had zero risk of mislabeling known IDs; the new code introduces ambient correctness coupled to ID naming conventions. The right structure is: explicit map first, heuristic only as fallback for unknown IDs — which is exactly what the *old* code did. The refactor moved in the wrong direction.

dissents.topic: Severity of removing DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES entry for category__in

positions.position: The PR explicitly advertises generic active filter badges; removing the category badge config while adding a category filter directly contradicts the description and likely breaks the UI affordance for clearing category filters.

positions.persona: P1 — likely covered by generic fallback
positions.position: DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES is described as defaults; the new badge component may auto-handle unmapped keys with the labelFormatter. Without seeing active-filter-badge.tsx full implementation, this is plausibly intentional cleanup, not a regression.

Two keys with the same value in an ordinal map is a code smell — it suggests the upstream is inconsistent and the patch papers over the problem at the constant rather than at the boundary. Normalize at the API adapter layer.
Two keys mapping to the same rank cost nothing at runtime; sorts remain stable. It's a one-line fix for a real cross-API inconsistency and over-engineering normalization isn't worth it here.

review.summary: This PR ships a Risk Radar visualization, a category filter for findings, a brand rename to 'Prowler ThreatScore', and a shared lib/categories.ts utility. The functional surface is reasonable, but several concerns warrant attention before merge: (1) the active-filter badge config for `category__in` was deleted in the same PR that adds the Category filter, which appears to contradict the PR description and may regress the active-filter-badge UX; (2) the refactor of getCategoryLabel replaced an explicit, correct label map with heuristics that will mislabel un-hyphenated compound IDs like 'trustboundaries' and any longer acronyms (HTTPS, SAML); (3) duplicating 'Info: 4' next to 'Informational: 4' in SEVERITY_ORDER smells like normalization that belongs at the API adapter boundary; (4) the HorizontalBarChart recomputes maxValue inside the row map and now uses two different denominators for bar width vs displayed percentage, creating a visual/data mismatch. Most issues are P1 quality concerns rather than merge-blockers; the badge regression is the most likely candidate to elevate to P0 after verifying behavior in the running app.
